violations.why: The ISR can increment v_pylon between the task's two reads, so the two accesses use different indices.
When i==2 the task writes v_vessel[2], the ISR can overwrite it, and the task then reads back the ISR's value.
The else branch can also write v_vessel[2], since i is unconstrained and may equal 2 by assumption of rand. The ISR can overwrite it before the read at line 31.
